Without the matching post-teleport position, the preliminary oracle sent sync, center and old forgets but did not complete the destination window.
observed_semantics: Full initial and far destination windows contain 49 unique columns of the centered 7x7 window; one-column movement adds seven new columns.
Both oracles observed sync then cache center then old forgets before destination batch start on distant teleports. One-column movement observed center then old forgets before batches.
Every batch was nonnested and finished with exactly its received chunk count; packet bodies passed independent full chunk/light decoding.
Initial negative cache centers match floor division of absolute position, and negative destination (-311.5,71,-311.5) centers at (-20,-20).
scope_limits: Exact chunk order, batch sizes, time to completion and scheduling are descriptive observations, not required constants.

Existing Go near-window prune retains an extra border and its final window commit pumps before forgetting; this responsiveness slice preserves those existing behaviors rather than claiming exact vanilla packet interleaving or near-prune parity.
Observer timing includes transport and client scheduling; deterministic scheduler tests separately establish complete-unit interleaving.
Dimension invalidation wire checks reuse the existing measured 16-section nether and 24-section overworld grammar; no new vanilla dimension-transition observation is claimed.
